departure_lines: Left the warmth of the bed.
Set out. The work won't find itself.
Stepped off the bed. The bed will be here when I get back.
Out into the morning, which had already started without me.
The bed was warm. Left it anyway.
Set out with the bag light. Should be heavier coming home.
Followed my own scent backward to where I last did this work. Started there.
Took one last look at the bed. The bed will be the bed.
Set out early. The cold hadn't lifted yet.
recall_lines: Heard the whistle. Turned where I was standing.
Called home. Did not argue. Went.
Whistle through the dark, a long way off. Followed it.
Got the recall. Set down what I was doing.
Coming back. The work will keep.
Recalled mid-step. Took the same step home instead.
Heard the signal. Dropped it and walked.
Called back. Set it all down.
abandoned_lines: Bed gone. Came home to nothing.
Home is no longer where I left it. Will wait nearby.
Something happened at the bed. Came back to find it gone.
No bed to return to. Stood in the place where it had been.
Expedition over. The bed is not here.
Found the place where the bed was. Nothing left of it.
Walked back expecting the bed. The bed was not there.
death_lines: Walked out. Did not walk in.
Somewhere out there. Will be out there a long time.
failure_lines: Came back with nothing. Sat by the bed for a long time.
Came back empty. Did not explain.
Nothing to show. Nothing to say.
Walked home with the bag the same weight it went out.
Empty. The work did not happen. The walking did.
No catch, no haul, no story worth telling. Came home anyway.
Bag light, ears down. The bed forgave it.
Came home with my own scent on me and nothing else.
Sometimes that's what the job looks like.
Sat on the bed a long while. The bed did not ask any questions.
Came back empty. The bag confirmed it.
success_lines: Came back slower than expected. Came back.
Bag full. Paws sore. A good kind of sore.
Came home heavier than I went out. The right kind of heavier.
Set the bag down. Set it down with both paws. It was that kind.
Heavy bag. Good kind of heavy.
A good day's haul. The kind of day that pays for the bad ones.
Third trip this week. The route knows me now.
Long walk. Good bag. Good bed.
Came home and the bed smelled the way I had hoped it would.
Came back the way I went out, only slower. The bag was the difference.
arrival_lines: Stepped over the threshold. The day was done.
Walked the last stretch with my nose. Did not need eyes.
The bed. Same as I left it.
Returned. The bed was patient about it.
Smelled home before I saw it. Kept walking.
Stepped onto the bed. Smelled like home. Was home.
The smell hit before the shape did. Came the rest of the way anyway.
low_resources_lines: Supplies thin. The work is not.
Worse shape than yesterday. Yesterday is not today.
Something went wrong back there. Not dwelling on it.
Hungry, tired, far from home. Three out of three. Pushing on.
Bag near empty. Body near empty. Heart still has some.
The work is heavier than the bag. The bag is heavy.
Cut and limping. Walked it off as well as walks it off.
Out of food, out of patience, not yet out of work.
Drank from a puddle. The puddle had seen worse drinkers.
Counted the breaths. Made them last.
The dark side of a good expedition. Pushing through.
loot_loss_lines: Something fell. No time to go back for it.
Bag tore. Lost a piece. Did not look back.
Dropped something. Did not know what. Cannot afford to find out.
The bag is lighter now. Did not choose this.
Lost a piece on the way through. The way through did not slow.
The bag emptied a little. Not by my choosing.
Lost some weight off the bag. The lost weight had a name. Forgot it.
low_food_lines: Last of the food. Making it count.
Ate the last but one. Watching the bag now.
Food is nearly gone. The work is not.
Down to the last scrap. Hoping it stretches.
The food side of the bag is almost nothing now.
One left. After that, the bag is just weight.
Rationing. The last one always has to last longer than the ones before it.
Checked the bag. One piece. Did not put it back.
Almost out of food. Not yet out of ground to cover.
